title: Layer 1 — Physical
html:
Where raw bits travel as copper voltages, light pulses, or radio signals.

Definition

The Physical Layer is the hardware base of the network. It deals with the transmission and reception of unstructured raw data streams (bits) over physical media. It defines electrical voltages, light frequencies, connector shapes, cable specs, and transmission speeds.

PDU: Bit
Focus: Electrical/Optical Signals
Hardware: Hubs, Repeaters, Cables, Modems

Core Purpose & Function

Layer 1 has no understanding of packet headers, addresses, or applications. It is strictly concerned with sending a series of electrical or optical pulses representing "1" or "0" down a wire, and ensuring that a receiver interprets those physical pulses back into matching bits.

Key Responsibilities

  • Bit Representation: Defining how 1s and 0s are coded (e.g. changes in voltage levels, light brightness, or radio frequency phases).
  • Bandwidth & Data Rates: Governing the maximum bit rate (transmission speed in Mbps/Gbps) supported by a cable type.
  • Physical Media Specifications: Standardizing wire thicknesses, fiber core widths, connector shapes (like RJ45 plugs), and shielding specifications.
  • Line Configuration & Duplexing: Defining whether transmission is point-to-point, simplex (one-way), half-duplex, or full-duplex.

Common Physical Media

Medium TypeDescriptionTypical SpeedPros / Cons
Unshielded Twisted Pair (UTP)Copper wires twisted to reduce interference100 Mbps – 10 GbpsCheap, flexible, but short range (~100m)
Fiber Optic CableGlass strands transmitting light pulses1 Gbps – 100+ GbpsImmune to electromagnetic interference, long range
Coaxial CableShielded copper conductor10 – 100 MbpsResistant to noise, used for cable TV/broadband
Radio FrequenciesElectromagnetic waves traveling through airUp to 10 Gbps (Wi-Fi 7)No physical wires needed, but prone to walls/noise

Analogy: The Asphalt Roads & Highways

Amazon Analogy

The Physical Layer is the actual asphalt roads, physical bridges, and truck engines. It represents the physical tires rolling on the road. Without the asphalt, no delivery van can move. It doesn't know what's in the van or where it's going; it is just the physical conduit that allows travel.

Hardware & Physical Connectors

Pros
  • Establishes the physical link necessary for any network to function.
  • Fiber optics provide near-light-speed transmission over massive distances.
Cons
  • Vulnerable to physical damage (cuts, water leaks, severe weather).
  • Signal attenuation requires repeaters/amplifiers over long distances.
